idiom_name: application lock table inside a Fluent/SQLKit transaction (SwiftData and Core Data offer only optimistic merge policies)
implementation_notes: Neither SwiftData nor Core Data exposes a pessimistic row lock: they resolve conflicts after the fact through NSMergePolicy (error, mergeByPropertyStoreTrump, mergeByPropertyObjectTrump, overwrite, rollback), which is optimistic locking by another name. Vapor's Fluent query builder likewise ships no forUpdate - its documentation covers filters, joins, chunking and aggregates only - and SQLite, the usual local store, has no SELECT ... FOR UPDATE at all, taking the write lock with BEGIN IMMEDIATE instead. The pattern is therefore hand-written: a lock record with a unique lockable key is claimed and released inside Fluent/SQLKit transactions, with owner and timeout stored so the claim survives across requests; the classic structure is justified because no framework primitive can hold a claim across user think time.
pitfalls: The framework's default merge policy can silently overwrite fields (mergeByPropertyObjectTrump) - reaching for NSMergePolicy instead of a lock is an optimistic solution with different failure timing.
SQLite serialises writers wholesale, so the lock record is advisory: a second writer finds out only at COMMIT (SQLITE_BUSY), not at acquire time.
Task cancellation does not roll back a database transaction; the lock record must be cleaned up by the timeout sweep, never by assuming structured concurrency will tidy up.
